definition: A system component that directs incoming requests to different models (or model configurations) based on factors like task complexity, cost constraints, or required capability.
details: Model routing allows applications to balance cost and performance by sending simpler queries to smaller, cheaper models and reserving larger, more capable (and expensive) models for harder tasks.
story: Imagine teaching a friend to shoot a basketball. They miss, and you walk them backwards through the shot — elbow, wrist, release — to find what needs fixing. In plain words: A system component that directs incoming requests to different models (or model configurations) based on factors like task complexity, cost constraints, or required capability. Here is how it actually plays out: Model routing allows applications to balance cost and performance by sending simpler queries to smaller, cheaper models and reserving larger, more capable (and expensive) models for harder tasks. It is learning from every miss instead of repeating the same mistake. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Model Router.
